back: The TCP connection stays open for multiple request–response pairs, avoiding a new handshake each time. Requests are still serial within one connection.
Multiple concurrent request–response streams share one TCP connection. Frames from different streams are interleaved, so a slow response on one stream does not block others at the HTTP level.

front: What transport does HTTP/3 use and why?
back: QUIC over UDP. QUIC provides per-stream reliability, eliminating TCP-level HOL blocking, and integrates TLS 1.3 for a faster handshake.
QUIC connections are identified by a connection ID, not by IP:port. When a mobile client switches networks, the connection survives.
Safe = does not change server state (GET, HEAD). Idempotent = same result whether sent once or many times (GET, PUT, DELETE). POST is neither.

front: Why is PUT idempotent but POST is not?
back: PUT replaces a resource: doing it twice sets the same value. POST creates or triggers an action: doing it twice may create two resources.

A unique key the client sends with a POST request. The server stores it and, if the same key arrives again, returns the original response without re-processing. Prevents duplicate orders/payments on retry.
1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
The server is rate-limiting the client. Retry after the time indicated in the Retry-After header.
no-cache: cache the response but revalidate with the origin on every use. no-store: do not cache at all.
A fingerprint of the response body. The client sends If-None-Match: <etag> on subsequent requests. If unchanged, the server returns 304 Not Modified with no body.
public: any cache (browser, CDN, proxy) may store. private: only the end-user's browser may cache. Use private for user-specific data.
Include a hash in the filename (app.3f8a.js). Cache with max-age=31536000, immutable. When code changes, the filename changes, forcing a cache miss.
A Cache-Control directive that overrides max-age for shared caches (CDNs, reverse proxies) but not for the browser.
Returned when a conditional request (ETag or Last-Modified) shows the content has not changed. No body is sent, saving bandwidth. The client uses its cached copy.
